exact_statement: For a Boolean sign f on a finite or countable uniform product cube with finite Fourier entropy and influence, let delta_m be squared Fourier mass outside labels contained in [m], T_H its entropy contribution and T_I its degree-weighted mass. For m>=1 and delta_m<=1/8, g=sign E[f|X_1,...,X_m] with sign(0)=+1 obeys P(f!=g)<=delta_m/2, |I(f)-I(g)|<=m delta_m+T_I, and |H(f)-H(g)|<=T_H+h2(sqrt(2delta_m))+m sqrt(2delta_m). Thus affine compression/minimization gives an actual Boolean gstar of dimension at most m with D_K(gstar)>=D_K(f)-E_m(K), where E_m is the displayed entropy bound plus K(m delta_m+T_I), for every K>=0. Conversely for every nonconstant full-affine-span affine-influence-minimal finite Boolean seed g, taking t=2^k disjoint seed copies and activating their product on k zero controls yields actual full-span affine-influence-minimal F_k with L2 distance squared from 1 at most 4*2^-k, I(F_k)->I(g), H(F_k)->H(g), and |D_K(F_k)-D_K(g)|<=2^-k[(10+2K)k+15]. For every fixed spectral window the entropy and influence outside it tend to H(g) and I(g). Bounded influence and L2 convergence therefore do not supply the entropy/influence tail control needed for optimizer arguments. No infinite optimizer or universally paid pair is asserted.
hypotheses: Normalized real Walsh coefficients; uniform finite or countable product; entropy bits; K>=0
Approximation requires finite H,I, m>=1 and explicitly delta_m<=1/8; zero coefficients and sign ties have stated conventions
Escape requires a fixed nonconstant finite Boolean seed with full affine spectral span and full affine influence minimality; k>=2, t=2^k, controls precede all data coordinates
proof_dependencies: Elementary Parseval, conditional variance, maximal finite-alphabet coupling and actual signed activation coefficients
A002-ACTIVATED-FULL-AFFINE-RESET-LEDGER@1 and A055 activation context motivate the construction; displayed activation profile and preservation are rederived
